slides.heading: Depth First Search
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Easy · Graphs
slides.narration: Let's solve Depth First Search, an easy graphs problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Given a tree-like graph of named nodes, return names in DFS (pre-order) order.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Given a tree-like graph of named nodes, return names in DFS (pre-order) order.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Depth-first search visits a node, then fully explores each child before moving to the next sibling.
slides.narration: Depth-first search visits a node, then fully explores each child before moving to the next sibling.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: DFS is already linear: O(V + E)
Alternative: BFS gives a different (level) order
Iterative DFS needs children pushed in reverse
slides.narration: Depth-first search is already linear in vertices plus edges. What matters is the order: we go as deep as possible before backtracking, unlike breadth-first search, which goes level by level.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 2. Recurse into each child in order
slides.narration: Step by step. First, append the node's name. Second, recurse into each child in order. Third, return the collected list.

slides.narration: We visit A and append it. Then we dive into its first child before touching its siblings.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: The method appends this node's name, then calls depth-first search on each child in order, passing the same list, and returns it.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of v plus e. Space is O of v.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
bullets: Child order matters: left to right
Iterative: push children reversed onto the stack
General graphs need a visited set (trees don't)
slides.narration: Children must be visited left to right. If you use an explicit stack, push children in reverse. On general graphs, add a visited set to avoid cycles.

slides.heading: Interview tips & follow-ups
bullets: Follow-up: detect a cycle, topological sort
slides.narration: Know both the recursive and iterative versions; DFS underpins cycle detection and topological sort.

slides.heading: Recap
bullets: Depth-first search visits a node, then fully explores each child before moving to the next sibling.
